title: Runbook: safe automation hooks for batching/caching commits
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design and ship API and SDK primitives to support safe, replayable automation for batching and KV-cache recommendations. The goal is to provide exactly-once semantics (or clear compensating actions) for applying optimization recommendations produced by Redwood Optimize: dry-run/preview, prepare/commit/abort flows, idempotency keys, webhook delivery guarantees, DLQ and operator remediation, and an SDK contract for integrators (partners and internal automations).
acceptance_criteria: Preview endpoint: recommendations can be validated with a dry-run that returns simulated cost/latency delta without mutating config
Two-phase apply API: /optimize/prepare -> returns proposal ID and lock token; /optimize/commit accepts token and makes change; /optimize/abort releases lock and records aborted snapshot
Idempotency: apply/commit endpoints accept an idempotency key; duplicate retries are deduplicated and safe

Webhook contract: delivery semantics documented (at-least-once), each event includes dedupe key, proposal ID, snapshot URL and replay URL; Consumer SDK helpers for exactly-once processing using checkpointing
Replayability: every proposal stores immutable snapshot and action plan accessible via signed URL for audit and rollback
Audit & observability: every apply/commit/abort recorded in audit log with actor, timestamps, diff, and cost estimate; Console shows per-proposal timeline
Failure modes: documented DLQ behavior and operator runbook for partial application and compensating rollback
E2E tests and integration tests cover retry scenarios, concurrent prepare/commit attempts, and webhook redelivery with duplicate events
technical_notes: Use optimistic lock token returned by prepare to ensure commit only succeeds if snapshot matches (etag semantics)
Idempotency keys stored with TTL equal to retention window; key+action determine dedupe; store result and response for quick replay
Snapshots are immutable JSON blobs with versioned schema and content-addressed storage; keep at least 30 days for rollback
Webhooks: sign payload with HMAC; include headers X-Redwood-Signature and X-Redwood-Event; include event_id for dedupe
SDK primitives: PrepareProposal, CommitProposal, AbortProposal, FetchProposalSnapshot, AckWebhookWithCheckpoint; implement exponential backoff with jitter for retries
DLQ: events that fail consumer processing after N retries are placed into per-customer DLQ with operator alert; include auto-retry policy configurable per workspace
Compatibility: maintain existing Optimize endpoints; new endpoints behind feature flag workspace.optimize_new_apply_flow
Security: proposal snapshots access-controlled; signed URLs expire and require console-level audit when fetched; KMS-wrapped when including sensitive routing config
implementation_plan: API design draft and review: define request/response shapes for prepare/commit/abort, preview, and webhook payloads
Schema design: proposal snapshot format, etag generation, idempotency store schema
Server: implement prepare endpoint, snapshot persistence, and idempotency key write path
Server: implement commit and abort with optimistic locking and side-effects orchestration (apply to config store, trigger infra hooks)
Webhook bridge: emitter with signed payloads and retry/dedup logic; expose DLQ UI hooks
SDK: publish JS and Python helpers for integrators (idempotency helpers, safe retry wrappers, webhook consumer client)
Console: proposal timeline UI, preview diff, manual rollback button tied to abort flow
Testing: unit tests, integration tests with fake webhook consumers, chaos testing for retries and partial failures
Docs & runbook: public API docs, internal runbooks for operators and SRE, and release notes
risks: Partial application risk if external systems (e.g., Dedicated config applier) accept partial changes; mitigated by transactional apply where possible and compensating rollback flows
Idempotency key exhaustion or collisions if clients misuse predictable keys; recommend UUIDv4 and validate key length
Schema drift on snapshots could break old rollback clients; mitigate with versioned snapshots and migration helpers
Increased storage for proposal snapshots; need quota controls and retention policy
Webhook consumer reliability: partner integrations may mis-handle duplicates leading to customer impact; provide SDK and clear guidance
qa_plan: Unit tests for idempotency store behavior (duplicate prepare/commit retries)
Integration tests simulating webhook redelivery, consumer ack, and DLQ behaviour
Simulate concurrent prepare/commit from two actors to validate optimistic locking
Chaos tests: intermittent failures in commit path to ensure abort/rollback path leaves system consistent
Load test: create 10k proposals/day retention to verify snapshot store and idempotency TTL scaling
deployment_steps: Deploy API behind feature flag in staging; enable for internal orgs only
Run integration tests with Canary workspace using internal SDK helper
Open rollout: enable for 5% of orgs and monitor errors, latency, and DLQ growth
If metrics stable for 48h, increase to 25%, then 100% following sign-off
Deprecate legacy one-shot apply endpoint after 2 release cycles with migration guide
